title: REF-GATED-RUBRIC: is rubric value CONDITIONAL on the reference being right? (the specific-judges line, redirected; 3,594 calls)
question: A 2x2 run fresh in one session: 900 matches where the grok reference is WRONG and 899 where it is CORRECT (drawn from answer-disagreeing key-decidable pairs), each judged with the anchor rubric alone and with the RK-1b data-only leaf card, paired, single order, grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning: (1) the INTERACTION (card effect in stratum B minus A) with a bootstrap CI excluding zero; (2) stratum A null at adequate power; (3) stratum B replicates RK-1b; (4) the decisiveness split.

registration.program_lines: docs/rubric_v2_design.md L331-L363 (registration) and L364-L400 (outcome); no programme section (the rubric line is recorded in rubric_v2_design.md)
registration.heading: ## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any call) — REF-GATED-RUBRIC: is rubric value conditional on the reference being right?
outcome_heading: docs/rubric_v2_design.md L364: - **REF-GATED-RUBRIC OUTCOME (2026-09-14): the registered interaction FAILS, both cells individually reproduce RUBRIC-STRATA, and the failure is my sampling error rather than a property of the world.**

go: under the 4,000-match rule (1,800 matches, 3,600 calls registered; 3,594 posted)

review.file: no separate review file (pre-dates docs/reviews/); the ledger audit's C-6 (population mismatch) is the class the registration itself fell into, named in the outcome
review.verdict: (1) NOT CONFIRMED; (2) (3) (4) INFORMATIVE: stratum A definitively null at good power, stratum B replicates RK-1b, the card buys discrimination there

criteria.text: PRIMARY: the interaction (card's paired effect in stratum B minus stratum A) positive with a bootstrap CI excluding zero
criteria.value: +0.013, bootstrap 95% [-0.008, +0.036]: NOT CONFIRMED; a sampling error of the registration: both strata drawn from answer-DISAGREEING pairs (the shipped filter) while RUBRIC-STRATA was unfiltered, so the reference-correct baseline is 0.969 here vs 0.930 there and the card had only 3.1pp of ceiling (the audit's C-6 class)

criteria.text: stratum A (reference WRONG) alone against zero, null at adequate power
criteria.value: 0.389 vs 0.389, +0.000, 40:40 discordant on 899 matches, McNemar p 1.000; MDE ~2.0pp at a 0.089 discordance rate: the card moves 80 verdicts and they cancel exactly; the n = 127 null in RUBRIC-STRATA was not a fluke

criteria.text: stratum B (reference CORRECT) replicates RK-1b's +1.3 to +1.7pp on a fresh sample and session
criteria.value: 0.969 -> 0.982, +1.3pp, 3:15, p 0.0075 (the original RK-1b PASS depended on which of three byte-identical control sessions was drawn; this is a clean independent replication)

criteria.text: DECISIVENESS SPLIT: decisive-and-correct and correct-given-committed for all four cells
criteria.value: stratum B: ties 1.0% -> 0.6%, correct-given-committed 0.979 -> 0.988 (about 0.9pp of the 1.3pp is better judging: DISCRIMINATION, the opposite of the RK-1b anatomy); stratum A: ties 0.101 -> 0.103, committed 0.433 -> 0.434 (nothing moves)

predictions.text: interaction +1.5 to +3pp with a CI excluding zero
the card's effect in stratum B is mostly decisiveness

falsifier.text: IF the interaction is null, RUBRIC-STRATA was noise and the rubric line stays closed where it was; IF confirmed, the line is REDIRECTED (a cell-specific judge means a cell-specific REFERENCE)
falsifier.note: the interaction is unconfirmed as a registered test; the directional claim stands on its components: a rubric cannot substitute for a reference, it can only improve the use of one that already works (+1.3pp where right, p 0.0075; exactly nothing where wrong, 40:40 at ~2pp resolution); the clean rerun (reference-correct stratum drawn WITHOUT the disagreement filter, 3,600 calls) is not worth spending

numbers_of_record.run: 3,594 calls, 0 errors; 900 + 899 matches; strata from the 7,691 answer-disagreeing key-decidable pairs on the 481 reference-wrong pool questions and the reference-correct questions
numbers_of_record.headroom: reference-correct baseline 0.969 here vs 0.930 in RUBRIC-STRATA (3.1pp of ceiling)

sentence_of_record: REF-GATED-RUBRIC (2026-09-14, 3,594 calls): the registered interaction FAILS (+0.013 [-0.008, +0.036]) and the failure is the registration's sampling error (both strata drawn from answer-disagreeing pairs, leaving the card 3.1pp of ceiling: the audit's C-6 class); both cells individually reproduce RUBRIC-STRATA: where the reference is WRONG the card gives +0.000 with 40:40 discordant on 899 matches (definitively null at ~2pp resolution), where it is RIGHT it replicates RK-1b on a fresh sample and session (+1.3pp, 3:15, p = 0.0075) and buys DISCRIMINATION, not decisiveness (correct-given-committed 0.979 -> 0.988). The directional claim stands on its components: a rubric cannot substitute for a reference, only improve the use of one that works; the formal interaction is unconfirmed and must be quoted as such.

plain_description.what: A 2x2 judged run (3,594 calls). It compares matches where the reference answer is wrong with matches where it is right, each judged with and without a cell-specific rubric card.
plain_description.why: Tests whether a rubric only helps when the judge's reference is correct, which decides whether a cell-specific judge needs a cell-specific rubric or a cell-specific reference.
plain_description.information: Tells where to invest to make judges better per cell. Result: the registered interaction test FAILED (not confirmed), largely because of how the samples were drawn. Taken separately, the rubric does exactly nothing when the reference is wrong, and gives a small gain (+1.3pp) when it is right. Direction: a rubric cannot replace a good reference, it can only sharpen one that works. Older judged set, now classed as history.
